title: High school orchestra: playing bass by ear, switching from violin at fourteen
summary: Looking at a photo of the school orchestra, Stewart says he played bass without reading, was shown how to tune it, and switched from violin at about fourteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Now, when you were -- like in this program here, in this tribute to Erroll Garner that you did in March of 1978, there's a photograph of you in the high school orchestra in New Jersey, in Englewood, New Jersey. And in the photograph there's like this one, two, there are three -- three colored people, and one of them was you, playing with the bass. The guy holding the drum -- there's another guy sitting behind the saxophones.
Now, what -- you were playing the bass by then.

I was playing the bass, at least trying to. I didn't know one note from the other, but I had a pretty good ear, you know, and I managed to get by. One of the fiddle players in the school orchestra, he had to show me how to even tune the bass, which is altogether reverse from the little violin, which -- I had studied, you know, but I didn't know exactly how the bass was supposed to be tuned.
Well, you -- now, you were playing the -- you began playing the violin when you were seven, you said.
So now, when did you switch over to the bass?
Oh, I switched over, I'd say, when I was about 14.
14. So you played the violin for about seven years before you --
-- before you started playing the bass.
And so you began to become interested in the bass from radio broadcasts.
